Render a gsm.viz tiles heatmap

Source: R/tiles.R
tiles.Rd

Thin htmlwidget over gsmViz.default.tiles, an HTML-table heatmap with one row per y value, one column per x value, and optional in-place expandable columns. spec maps 1:1 to the JS spec; gsm.viz's tiles documentation is the source of truth for its keys.

Usage

tiles(
  data,
  spec,
  metadata = list(),
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  elementId = NULL,
  bDebug = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

data.frame One row per (row, column) cell.

spec

list Chart specification. spec$mapping$x and spec$mapping$y are required and must name columns of data. When spec$expand is set, spec$expand$data must be a data.frame holding the mapping$x, mapping$y and expand$mapping$x columns.

metadata

list Named list of report keys (e.g. chartId) echoed in event payloads. chartId also becomes the widget element's id outside Shiny.

width, height, elementId

Standard htmlwidgets arguments.

bDebug

logical Log the payload to the browser console.

Value

A tiles htmlwidget.

Details

data and spec$expand$data travel column-wise (one JSON array per column) and are rebuilt into row objects in the browser, which keeps large detail tables a fraction of their rows-wise size. NA arrives as null.

Every interaction dispatches a bubbling gsm-viz-select CustomEvent on the widget element, then runs any user js_hook() callback (called with this set to the widget element). Event detail shapes:

  • cell click: {type: "click", chartId, datum, metadata}

  • row header click: {type: "rowclick", chartId, y, rows, metadata}

  • column expand/collapse: {type: "expand", chartId, x, expanded, metadata}

Row header clicks do not select the row; call el.gsmChart.helpers.selectRow(el.gsmChart, y) to do so. The chart object is stored on the widget element as el.gsmChart and the metadata as el.gsmMeta.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  subjid = c("P1", "P1", "P2"),
  vital = c("Pulse", "SBP", "Pulse"),
  flag = c("Red", "Green", "Amber")
)
tiles(
  df,
  list(
    mapping = list(x = "vital", y = "subjid", fill = "flag"),
    scales = list(
      fill = list(colors = list(Green = "#3DAF06", Amber = "#FEAA02", Red = "#FF5859"))
    )
  )
)
